title: Accuracy at a Goldreich–Levin stage
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube, let $\tau$ be rational with $0<\tau\leq1$, and let $W(J,S)$ be a rational estimate for each coordinate subset $J$ and each $S\subseteq J$. Choose $k<n$ and a family $A$ of subsets of the coordinates. Put $J=\{0,\ldots,k\}$. The estimate is accurate at stage $k$ for $A$ if, for every Goldreich–Levin candidate $S$ formed from coordinate $k$ and the active family $A$, its error $|W(J,S')-\widehat W_f(J,S')|$ on the restricted Fourier weight is less than $\tau^2/4$, where $S'$ is the candidate's free-frequency part within $J$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube
$W(J,S)$ is rational for every coordinate subset $J$ and every $S\subseteq J$
$A$ is a finite family of subsets of the coordinates
The error bound holds for every candidate generated from coordinate $k$ and $A$
